subtitle: Guilds, Monks and the Stone Ledger of the Deccan

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a rock-cut façade with donor standing beside a carved pillar
panels.action: Satavahana Guild Donor stands beside a freshly carved stone pillar before a rock-cut cave, hand resting on the pillar, looking up toward rows of monastic cells carved into the cliff face.

dialogue.text: In the Satavahana Deccan, merchants and guilds carved their gifts into stone, turning trade and coin into monasteries that outlived kings.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन दक्खिन में व्यापारी और श्रेणियाँ दान पत्थर पर लिखवाते, सौदे और सिक्के को राजाओं से भी टिकाऊ विहारों में बदल देते थे।

panels.shot: broad aerial establishing shot over a rocky Deccan plateau
panels.action: The Deccan plateau stretches under a hazy sky, with winding trade paths, scattered villages, and distant river valleys hinting at routes leading toward Nasik, Karla, Kanheri, Sanchi and Amaravati.

dialogue.text: From the rocky spine of the Deccan, paths ran to ports and plains, carrying cotton, spices and stone across Satavahana lands.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन की पथरीली रीढ़ से राहें बंदरगाहों और मैदानी इलाकों तक जातीं, कपास, मसाले और पत्थर सातवाहन भूमि भर में बहते रहते।

panels.shot: mid shot at ground level inside a bustling bazaar street
panels.action: Satavahana Guild Donor walks through a crowded market street with stalls of textiles, metalware and pottery, passing groups of artisans and traders weighing coins and goods.

dialogue.text: In bazaar streets, shrenis—organized circles of craftsmen and traders—wove their fortunes from workshop, caravan and ship.

i18n.hi: बाज़ार गलियों में श्रेणियाँ—कर्मकारों और व्यापारियों के संगठित समूह—कारखानों, काफिलों और जहाज़ों से अपनी किस्मत बुनते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on hands over a small balance scale
panels.action: The Guild Donor’s hands carefully place rounded lead and copper coins on a small balance scale on a wooden counter, with cloth bundles and account tablets nearby.

dialogue.text: Lead, copper and potin coins passed across their palms, practical tokens suited to a land where metal and trust carried trade.

i18n.hi: सीसा, ताँबा और पोटिन के सिक्के उनकी हथेलियों से गुजरते, ऐसे ढले टोकन जो उस देस के लिए बने थे जहाँ धातु और भरोसा ही व्यापार ढोते थे।

panels.shot: medium interior of a guild meeting in a pillared hall
panels.action: Satavahana Guild Donor sits among fellow merchants in a simple pillared hall, with ledgers and small coin heaps between them as they discuss, faces serious and intent.

dialogue.text: Within their halls, guild elders weighed more than metal. They weighed risk, routes, and how to make merit endure beyond a single lifetime.

i18n.hi: अपनी सभाओं में श्रेणी-मुखिया सिर्फ धातु नहीं तौलते, जोखिम, रास्ते और ऐसा पुण्य तौलते जो एक जनम से आगे टिके।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a cliff with rock-cut caves at Nasik
panels.action: The Guild Donor stands at the foot of Nasik’s cliff, gazing up at rows of rock-cut caves and façades, with monks moving quietly along carved verandas.

dialogue.text: Above the trade routes, at Nasik, artisans had carved the rock itself into monasteries, their walls cool, their verandas open to wind and pilgrims.

i18n.hi: व्यापार-पथों के ऊपर, नासिक में कारीगरों ने चट्टान को ही विहार बना डाला, ठंडी दीवारें, हवा और यात्रियों से भरी खुली बरामदे।

panels.shot: medium shot at Karla cave entrance with chaitya arch in background
panels.action: Satavahana Guild Donor stands near the great chaitya entrance at Karla, shadowed by towering rock-cut pillars and a vaulted arch leading into the dark hall beyond.

dialogue.text: At Karla, the mountain sheltered a vast chaitya hall, raised not only by kings, but by merchants, monks, nuns and guilds whose names clung to the stone.

i18n.hi: कार्ला में पहाड़ ने एक विशाल चैत्य-गृह को ढाँप रखा था, जो सिर्फ राजाओं ने नहीं, बल्कि उन व्यापारियों, भिक्षुओं, भिक्षुणियों और श्रेणियों ने उठाया था जिनके नाम पत्थर से चिपके रहे।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of Karla’s chaitya hall with pillars receding in perspective
panels.action: Inside the chaitya, the Guild Donor stands small amid parallel rows of carved pillars leading to a stupa, light filtering from the entrance onto smooth stone surfaces.

dialogue.text: Within, pillars marched like stone trees to the stupa. On their bases, early Brahmi letters recorded gifts: a column, a cell, a cistern, a village.

i18n.hi: अंदर, स्तम्भ स्तूप तक पत्थर के पेड़ों की कतार जैसे खड़े थे। उनके आधार पर ब्राह्मी के शुरुआती अक्षर चढ़ावे लिखते: एक स्तम्भ, एक कुटी, एक कुंड, एक गाँव।

panels.shot: tight close-up of a pillar base and a mason chiseling
panels.action: The Guild Donor stands beside a stonemason who kneels at a pillar base, chisel poised to cut neat Brahmi characters into a smooth prepared panel.

dialogue.text: Here the stone was ledger and witness. A mason’s hand, a merchant’s coin, a few lines of script bound them to a community of monks.

i18n.hi: यहाँ पत्थर ही बही भी था और गवाह भी। एक राजमिस्त्री का हाथ, एक व्यापारी का सिक्का, कुछ पंक्तियाँ—और वे सब भिक्षु-संघ से बँध जाते।

panels.shot: close-up on Guild Donor’s thoughtful face in profile
panels.action: The Guild Donor’s face is shown in profile, eyes lowered in focused thought as distant chanting from monks in the background drifts through the cave.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_guild_donors
dialogue.text: A pillar will stand longer than my warehouse. Let it carry our name.

i18n.hi: मेरी कोठार से ज़्यादा यह स्तम्भ टिकेगा। इसी पर हमारा नाम रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot at a Kanheri cistern with carved channel
panels.action: At Kanheri, the Guild Donor inspects a rock-cut water cistern fed by a carved channel, with monks nearby drawing water with simple pots.

dialogue.text: Nasik, Karla, Kanheri—each cliff bore proof that wealth could become water, shelter, and quiet cells for meditation.

i18n.hi: नासिक, कार्ला, कन्हेरी—हर चट्टान गवाही देती थी कि दौलत पानी, आसरा और ध्यान की शांत कुटियों में बदल सकती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a monk and nun receiving the donor at cave entrance
panels.action: A monk and a nun stand at the entrance of a cave, palms joined in greeting, as the Guild Donor bows slightly, holding a small pouch of coins and a palm-leaf record.

dialogue.text: Inscription after inscription speaks of monks and nuns, of laymen and laywomen, receiving gifts that bound householders to the sangha.

i18n.hi: एक के बाद एक लेख में भिक्षु-भिक्षुणियों, गृहस्थ पुरुषों और स्त्रियों के दान दर्ज हैं, जो गृहस्थों को संघ से बाँध देते थे।

panels.shot: interior meeting shot with monk, nun and donor seated on floor
panels.action: Inside a dim cave cell, the Guild Donor sits cross-legged opposite the monk and nun, a small heap of coins between them and an unfurled palm-leaf list of endowment terms.

dialogue.text: Gregory Schopen would later read these stones as contracts: endowments for lamps, for meals, for robes, tied to named donors and defined rights.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद में ग्रेगरी शोपेन ने इन पत्थरों को अनुबंध की तरह पढ़ा: दीप, भोजन, वस्त्रों के लिए दान, जिनमें दाताओं के नाम और अधिकार साफ़ लिखे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on a palm-leaf listing an endowment
panels.action: A palm-leaf manuscript lies on a low wooden board, lines of script indicating allocations for food, robes and maintenance, while the Guild Donor’s hand rests thoughtfully beside it.

dialogue.text: The gift was not vague piety. It was specific: so many coins, for such and such purpose, secured against land or income, with immunities carefully phrased.

i18n.hi: दान कोई धुंधली भक्ति नहीं था। सब तय था: इतने सिक्के, ऐसे काम के लिए, ज़मीन या आमदनी पर टिके, और छूटें साफ़ शब्दों में दर्ज।

panels.shot: medium shot outside Sanchi stupa railings with artisans working
panels.action: At Sanchi, the Guild Donor walks along the stone railings of a stupa where artisans carve panels, while a fellow merchant points out blank spaces awaiting dedicatory panels.

dialogue.text: At Sanchi, railings and gateways bore similar traces: the names of donors—guilds, officials, royal women—spoke where the king’s voice fell silent.

i18n.hi: सांची में भी रेलिंग और फाटकों पर वही निशान थे: दाताओं के नाम—श्रेणियाँ, अधिकारी, राजमहिला—वहीं बोलते जहाँ राजा की आवाज़ थम जाती थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Amaravati stupa with sculpted drum and donors below
panels.action: The Guild Donor stands before the great stupa at Amaravati, its carved drum and panels rising above, while other donors consult with sculptors at the base.

dialogue.text: At Amaravati, carved stone drums and panels sang of maritime wealth, of caravans and ships, of a coastal world where guilds carried both Buddha’s image and their own names.

i18n.hi: अमरावती में नक्काशीदार पत्थर-ढोल और पट्ट समुद्री दौलत, काफिलों और जहाज़ों का गीत थे—ऐसा तट जहाँ श्रेणियाँ बुद्ध की छवि के साथ अपना नाम भी ढोती थीं।

panels.shot: close-up of Guild Donor placing coins into a small chest near a stupa
panels.action: Near a small shrine, the Guild Donor gently places several coins into a wooden chest while looking toward the stupa, a quiet resolve on his face.

dialogue.speaker: satavahana_guild_donors
dialogue.text: Let this support lamps and meals for the community, as long as coins endure.

i18n.hi: यह दान संघ के दीप और भोजन चलाए, जब तक सिक्के चलते रहें।

panels.shot: tight close-up of Brahmi inscription being finished with chisel
panels.action: The mason’s chisel bites into stone as the final Brahmi characters of a donor inscription are completed, with the Guild Donor’s shadow falling across the pillar base.

dialogue.text: Lüders would one day list such inscriptions, reading, line by line, the economy of devotion that royal eulogies barely mentioned.

i18n.hi: कभी ल्यूडर्स ने ऐसे लेखों की सूची बनाई, पंक्ति दर पंक्ति पढ़ते हुए उस भक्ति की अर्थव्यवस्था खोली जिसे राजस्तुति बस छूकर निकल जाती थी।

panels.shot: close shot of the finished inscription beside the donor’s hand
panels.action: The finished inscription runs in neat Brahmi lines along the pillar base, the Guild Donor’s fingertips touching the carved letters lightly.

dialogue.text: Each line fixed a relationship: between donor and monastery, between land and immunity, between worldly profit and the hope of merit.

i18n.hi: हर पंक्ति एक रिश्ता बाँधती थी: दाता और विहार के बीच, ज़मीन और छूट के बीच, लौकिक नफे और पुण्य की आस के बीच।

panels.shot: wide shot of monks using facilities endowed by donors
panels.action: Monks walk along verandas, study in cells, and draw water from cisterns at a cave complex, while the Guild Donor watches quietly from a shaded corner.

dialogue.text: As seasons passed, endowments fed the cloistered and the traveling, turning isolated caves into nodal points on Neelis’s web of routes and shrines.

i18n.hi: ऋतुओं के साथ ये दान स्थायी और घुमंतू दोनों संघों को खिलाते, अकेली गुफाओं को नीलीस के मार्गों और तीर्थों के जाल के नोड बना देते।

panels.shot: dissolve-like composition showing faint future scholars over the cave façade
panels.action: The Guild Donor stands before the same cave façade, while faint ghostly outlines of modern scholars with notebooks and measuring tools overlay the scene, studying the inscriptions.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, scholars traced these grooves, seeing not just devotion, but an economy where guilds, households and monasteries shared risk, surplus and memory.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद विद्वान इन्हीं लकीरों को पढ़ते, और सिर्फ भक्ति नहीं, बल्कि एक ऐसी अर्थव्यवस्था देखते जहाँ श्रेणियाँ, घर और विहार जोखिम, बचत और यादें बाँटते थे।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the donor walking away along a cliff path
panels.action: At dusk, the Guild Donor walks along a cliffside path away from the caves, the carved pillar and its inscription visible behind, framed against the darkening sky.

dialogue.text: In their names beside pillars, guild donors turned passing profit into lasting institutions, proving that public generosity can anchor communities long after the coins themselves are forgotten.

i18n.hi: अपने नाम स्तम्भों के साथ जोड़कर श्रेणी-दाताओं ने गुज़रते मुनाफे को टिकाऊ संस्थानों में बदला, दिखा दिया कि खुला दान समुदायों को तब तक थामे रख सकता है जब तक असली सिक्कों की याद भी मिट जाए।

title_i18n.en: The Name Carved Beside the Pillar
title_i18n.hi: स्तम्भ के पास खुदा हुआ नाम

subtitle_i18n.en: Guilds, Monks and the Stone Ledger of the Deccan
subtitle_i18n.hi: श्रेणियाँ, भिक्षु और दक्खिन की पत्थर की बही
